new_packages.label: תְּפִלָּה וּבִטּוּל
new_packages.reason: The torah teaches two levels of bittul in prayer: (1) not sensing another person, only 'I and HaShem alone'; (2) the deeper level from the Abba Shaul teaching — not even sensing oneself, only the King Himself. These concepts — tefillah, bittul, the King's Palace, the King Himself — all share the same essential nature: the dissolution of selfhood before the Divine during prayer.

proposed_bechina_edges.reason: Prayer in its proper form IS self-nullification — they share the same essential nature in this torah.
During prayer one stands in the King's Palace — prayer is the bechina of being in the King's presence.
The Palace is the place of nullification — standing there, one's selfhood dissolves.
In the Palace, only the King Himself remains — the Palace and the King are the same reality from two angles.

source_quotes: כִּי צָרִיךְ כָּל אָדָם בִּשְׁעַת תְּפִלָּתוֹ, שֶׁיְּצַיֵּר בְּדַעְתּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אֲנִי וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד
שֶׁמְּחֻיָּב הָאָדָם לְבַטֵּל עַצְמוֹ כָּל־כָּךְ בִּשְׁעַת הַתְּפִלָּה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַרְגִּישׁ אֲפִלּוּ אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל
מִי הוּא, הֲלֹא יֵשׁוּתוֹ נִתְבַּטֵּל, וְאֵין כָּאן אֶלָּא הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ

observations: Torah #103 has zero bechina edges in the existing dataset. However, the source text contains a coherent cluster of 4 concepts — prayer, self-nullification, the King's Palace, and the King Himself — all sharing the same essential nature (the dissolution of yeshut/selfhood before HaShem during prayer). These 4 concepts with their proposed 4 bechina edges form one independent thematic domain qualifying as a new package. The torah has no evil mirror — it is entirely about the positive aspiration of complete bittul in tefillah. Note: this is a short, focused teaching (Tinyana style), so a single package of moderate size is appropriate.
